Formula: Euler-Lagrange Equations of Motion
Exact Expression: \frac{d}{dt}\left( \frac{\partial L}{\partial \dot{q}_i} \right) - \frac{\partial L}{\partial q_i} = 0
Definitions: Fundamental differential equations of analytical mechanics determining the trajectory of a dynamical system that renders the action stationary.
Derivation/Reference: Leonhard Euler (1744) & Joseph-Louis Lagrange (1788)
Example: Simple harmonic oscillator: L = (1/2)m(x_dot)^2 - (1/2)k x^2 -> d/dt(m x_dot) - (-kx) = 0 -> m x_ddot + k x = 0
Domain: classical_mechanics
Assumptions: Holonomic constraints; Conservative forces derivable from a potential V(q)
Common Errors: Confusing Lagrangian L = T - V with Hamiltonian H = T + V
subject: Euler-Lagrange Equations of Motion
